thread:
mike: Quick design follow-up. RFC suggested adding a compact fence. I ran into a related problem: when we reject handoffs during compaction we create transient allocation hot spots and delayed frees pile up. Proposal: introduce an `evict_token` + `deferred_free_window_ms` on handoff so receiver can promise to honor a short defer window instead of outright rejecting. Thoughts?

sara: Nice idea. That would let callers choose softer semantics: either STRICT reject or SOFT defer. How would this interact with existing clients that don't know the fields?

anand: Minimal compatibility: add fields as optional in proto. Default behavior for old receivers = no-defer (i.e., current semantics). But router will only advertise `defer_capable` in pool metadata after receiver version >= X. Router should never send `evict_token/defer_window` to hosts that don't advertise capability.

mike: Implementation sketch: HandOffRequest { optional string evict_token; optional int32 deferred_free_window_ms; optional bool prefer_defer; } HandOffResponse { enum token_outcome { ACCEPT, DEFERED, REJECT }; token_outcome token_status; string token_reason; }

jia: If we use a token, where's the ground truth? Receiver records token id in local lease table with expiry = now + window. During compaction we skip reclaiming pages tied to active tokens. That reduces immediate failures but increases fragmentation risk. We need safety limits (max concurrent tokens per host).

sara: Ops question: what's the worst-case memory blowup? If caller keeps requesting defers we might exceed OOM thresholds. Need admission control: host-level token quota and cluster-level token throttle. Add metric `evict_token.outstanding` and circuit-breaker.

lucy: On the telemetry side: add histograms for `deferred_free_window_ms` and counters for `token.{issued|accepted|rejected|expired}`. Also log a warning if token expirations correlate with compaction fails.

anand: Router policy nuance: when choosing pool, if prefer_defer=true, prefer nodes with `defer_capacity>0`. If none available, fallback options: 1) send without token (best-effort), 2) reject at router with `NO_DEFER_AVAILABLE`. We should make this config-driven: `offload.defer_policy = [USE_BEST_EFFORT, FAIL_FAST, QUEUE]`. Default USE_BEST_EFFORT.

mike: Rollout plan: 1) proto + receiver plumbing + metrics, 2) add capability bit in pool registry, 3) router change behind feature flag that queries capability, 4) canary, 5) enable for hosted gradually, 6) dedicated: opt-in per-customer in Console.
\sj? sara: Typo in timeline but sgtm. For Dedicated, we should never flip opt-in without explicit consent. Add a console toggle and an audit banner.

jia: Tests: unit tests for token lease table, integration test for token expiry causing immediate reclamation, stress test that issues burst handoffs with prefer_defer=true and measures tail latency and fragmentation growth. Who owns stress test?

sara: I'll own the stress tests. Plan: job that does 50k small handoffs/s, toggles compaction, measures failed handoffs and overall resident set growth.

lucy: Migration for on-prem: pre-upgrade hook should populate token counters and ensure DB schema for token table. If not present, node will advertise defer_capable=false. Provide a helper script to backfill.

anand: Backpressure risk: callers might spin on rejected handoffs. Make router return a `RETRY_AFTER_MS` hint and a default jittered backoff. Also ensure client libs treat `DEFERED` as success (it got placement) while `REJECT` triggers fallback.

mike: API ergonomics: client SDKs should expose `offloadOptions: { preferDefer: bool, deferWindowMs: number }` and surface token_reason in logs. We'll add a standard set of reasons: `COMPACT_ACTIVE`, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `UNSUPPORTED`.

lucy: One more: security/observability. Token IDs should be unguessable (UUID-v4) and include creation_ts. Redact them in public logs.

sara: Agreed. Ops ask: can we avoid adding another per-page global state? Token table should be per-allocator-bucket, sharded, and memory-bounded. Add eviction policy to drop oldest tokens when over limit and record `token_dropped` metric.

anand: Let's also add a simulation in the perf lab that models token issuance and compaction windows; that'll help tune defaults for window_ms (start with 200-1000ms).

mike: I'll open a PR with proto + receiver-side token table + plumbing. Will include TTL GC and metrics. Target: proto + unit tests by Thursday, router gating + canary next week.

deply-bot: deploy-bot: Image built: runtime-offload:v2026.04.defer-token. Canary: prod-canary-03 at 2026-04-05T16:00Z.

sara: Perfect. Last asks: 1) doc in the Console explaining Dedicated opt-in and behavior, 2) add integration test asserting older clients still get accepted handoff when they don't send token.

mike: Will do. Thanks all. I'll paste the PR here once it's up. :thumbsup:
